We use a range of provenance in Ireland, some from within the same region as the planting, others from elsewhere in the island of Ireland in addition to some European continental provenances when native provenance stock does not meet supply demand.

Two species of birch are native to Ireland; downy birch (Betula pubescens) and silver birch (Betula pendula). Until recently, two factors have prevented the listing of birch as a recommended species; the poor stem quality of naturally regenerated birch and the poor survival and growth rates.
 The approach to develop sources of improved planting stock has been;

Locating the best examples of mature trees (plus trees) of these species on which to base  the improvement programme
Collecting scion wood from plus trees for vegetative propagation by grafting
Establishing clone banks to preserve the genotypes
Establishing seed orchards
Establishing progeny trials to assess the value of the trees as parents
